title: Recent advances in first-row transition metal clusters for photocatalytic water splitting
claim: Many manganese-cluster water-oxidation reports do not establish efficient photochemical water oxidation under a photosensitizer/electron-acceptor system.
explanation: The review distinguishes oxidation driven by added chemical oxidants or oxygen-atom donors from the relatively few Mn-cluster examples of photochemical oxygen evolution and also notes stability concerns.
scope: Mn-based cluster catalysts discussed as photosystem-II oxygen-evolving-complex mimics.
conditions: Comparison concerns chemical oxidants such as oxone, peroxide, hypochlorite, and Ce(IV), versus photochemical systems with a photosensitizer and electron acceptor.
caveats: This is a limitation of the reviewed examples, not a claim that Mn clusters cannot catalyze photochemical water oxidation.
